record.original_question: Let B be the P Bergman space of square P∞ integrable functions in D, that is, those functions f (z) = ∞ n=0 na z n for which n=1 n −1 |a |2 < ∞. A subspace S n is said to be invariant if zf ∈ S whenever f ∈ S. What are the invariant subspaces of B? The corresponding problem for H 2 was solved by Beurling [95] and uses the inner-outer factorisation of H p functions, a tool unavailable in the present context. (L. Zalcman)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D} = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| < 1\}$ denote the open unit disc. Define the Bergman space $B$ to be the Hilbert space of analytic functions
$$f(z) = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} a_n z^n$$
on $\mathbb{D}$ such that
$$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{|a_n|^2}{n} < \infty,$$
which is equivalent to $f$ being square-integrable on $\mathbb{D}$ with respect to area measure. A closed linear subspace $S \subseteq B$ is called invariant if $zf \in S$ whenever $f \in S$.

Provide a complete description (classification) of all invariant subspaces of $B$, analogous to Beurling's classification of the invariant subspaces of the Hardy space $H^2$ via inner-outer factorization.
artifact.status_search_result: A full Beurling-type classification of invariant subspaces of the Bergman space remains out of reach: the lattice is enormously rich (essentially every operator on a separable Hilbert space arises as a compression of the Bergman shift to a quotient of two invariant subspaces). Aleman, Richter, and Sundberg (Acta Math., 1996) proved a significant structural result — every invariant subspace $M$ of $A^2(\mathbb{D})$ is generated by its wandering subspace, $M = [M \ominus zM]$ — but a complete classification of invariant subspaces (and a satisfactory understanding of the wandering subspaces) is still open.

status_evidence.title: Beurling's theorem for the Bergman space
status_evidence.snippet: Aleman, Richter and Sundberg showed that if M is an invariant subspace of A^2(D), then M = [M ⊖ zM].
status_evidence.claim: A wandering-subspace generation theorem (a partial Beurling-type result) is established, but not a full classification.

status_evidence.title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in the Bergman Space
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing progress and remaining open problems concerning invariant subspaces of the Bergman space.
status_evidence.claim: Classification of invariant subspaces of the Bergman space remains an active area with open problems.
